transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm just here because I get distracted really easily. Like, I'll be working on something for school, maybe a dashboard project or whatever, and... I don't know, a Slack message will pop up, or I'll hear a song, or just think of something else entirely. And then I just completely lose track of what I was doing. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot when you're supposed to be sitting still, like in class or during meetings?

Yeah, I guess so. Um... like in portfolio reviews or meetings, I'll... I don't know, I usually bounce my leg or twist my rings. Sometimes click my pen. I don't really realize I'm doing it, just kind of shifting around in my chair until someone looks at me. So... yeah.
Do you notice these problems with distraction and restlessness in different places, like at home, school, or when you're out with friends, or does it mostly happen in one setting like school?
Um... I don't know. I guess it's just kind of everywhere. Like at home too, maybe. I haven't really thought about it that much.
When did you first start noticing these issues with distraction and restlessness? Were they present when you were younger, like in childhood or early adolescence?

Um... yeah, I guess it's been a while. Like, even back in elementary school. I don't really remember it all that well, but... my parents said my teachers would leave notes on my report cards. Just stuff about me rushing through my worksheets, or... not following directions, I guess. And talking too much during group work, like talking over people. 

My parents... they actually used to have to sit next to me when I did my homework back then. Because if they didn't, I'd just... I don't know, wander off or start doing something else instead of finishing it. So... yeah. It's been going on for a long time, I suppose.
